title: Tense Mountain
description: Choose present perfect or past simple forms, including negatives, questions and error correction.

questions.prompt: We ____ the castle two days ago.
questions.explanation: Two days ago is a finished past time, so use past simple.

questions.prompt: Hana ____ her poster, so she can hand it in now.
questions.explanation: A completed action with a result now uses has + past participle for Hana.

questions.prompt: ____ you ever ridden a horse?
questions.explanation: Ever asks about experience up to now: Have you ever + past participle?

questions.prompt: My brother ____ his homework yet.
questions.explanation: Use has not + past participle with yet; the past participle of do is done.

questions.prompt: Where ____ you go last Saturday?
questions.explanation: A question about a finished past time uses did + subject + base verb.

questions.prompt: They ____ a new display last month.
questions.explanation: Last month is finished, so use made, the past simple of make.

questions.prompt: I ____ that film before, so I know the ending.
questions.explanation: Before links the experience to now; use have + seen.

questions.prompt: She ____ to the club meeting yesterday.
questions.explanation: Yesterday requires past simple; after did not, use the base form come.

questions.prompt: ____ your sister ever visited this museum?
questions.explanation: Your sister is singular; use Has + subject + ever + past participle.

questions.prompt: We ____ lunch yet, so we are hungry.
questions.explanation: Use have not + had with yet; had is the past participle of have.

questions.prompt: I ____ this schoolbag since September, and I still use it.
questions.explanation: Since introduces a starting point continuing to now; have had is correct.

questions.prompt: Ruba ____ her bicycle for three years, and she still rides it.
questions.explanation: For three years and still show a situation continuing to now: has had.

questions.prompt: They ____ the competition in 2024.
questions.explanation: In 2024 is a finished past time, so use won.

questions.prompt: The classroom is ready now. We ____ all the chairs.
questions.explanation: The present result is important; use have + arranged.

questions.prompt: What time ____ the bus arrive yesterday?
questions.explanation: Use did for a question about yesterday.

questions.prompt: I have never ____ a formal speech.
questions.explanation: After have never, use the past participle given.

questions.prompt: Omar ____ his uncle last Friday.
questions.explanation: Last Friday requires past simple: met.

questions.prompt: We ____ the old letters yet.
questions.explanation: Yet calls for have not + past participle here; read keeps the same spelling.

questions.prompt: ____ you finish the model last night?
questions.explanation: Last night is a finished time; Did you finish is the correct question.

questions.prompt: My aunt has already ____ the tickets.
questions.explanation: The past participle of buy is bought.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We did went to the library yesterday.
We has gone to the library yesterday.
We have gone to the library yesterday.
We went to the library yesterday.
questions.explanation: Yesterday needs past simple; went is the past simple of go.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Have Mariam written her report yet?
Did Mariam written her report yet?
Has Mariam written her report yet?
Has Mariam wrote her report yet?
questions.explanation: Use Has with Mariam and the past participle written.

questions.prompt: Correct the sentence: He has ate his lunch.
questions.explanation: Present perfect uses has + past participle; eaten is correct.

questions.prompt: Correct the sentence: They did not visited us on Monday.
options: They did not visit us on Monday.
They has not visited us on Monday.
They have not visited us on Monday.
They did not visits us on Monday.
questions.explanation: After did not, use visit, the base verb.

questions.prompt: Which phrase clearly refers to a finished past time?
questions.explanation: Ago places an action at a finished point in the past.

questions.prompt: Which sentence asks about experience up to now?
options: Did you make a family tree yesterday?
Are you making a family tree now?
Will you make a family tree tomorrow?
Have you ever made a family tree?
questions.explanation: Have you ever asks about experience at any time before now.

questions.prompt: Complete both gaps: ____ you ever ____ an old coin?
questions.explanation: Use Have you ever + found, the past participle of find.

questions.prompt: Complete both gaps: When ____ she ____ the school last year?
questions.explanation: Last year needs did + subject + base form join.

questions.prompt: The shelves are empty now because the pupils ____ all the books to another room.
questions.explanation: The completed action explains the situation now: have moved.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with the correct negative form.
options: She has not choose a topic yet.
She has not chose a topic yet.
She have not chosen a topic yet.
She has not chosen a topic yet.
questions.explanation: Use has not + chosen, the past participle of choose.
